backbone_and_pretraining: ResNet-12; 'We utilized the ResNet-12 [9] based architecture for the feature extraction, following previous FSL methods [14, 35]. The feature extractor creates a 640-dimensional feature vector for an input image through the last average pooling layer. We pre-trained the extractor with a simple classifier to classify all classes in the base dataset. The classifier is a single fully-connected layer that creates logits of the classes.' (Sec. 4.2, p. 6). Supp. Sec. 1.1: 'The first pre-training is done up to 500 epochs using the whole base dataset, like regular supervised classification training.' (SGD, lr 0.1, momentum 0.9, wd 5e-4, 500 epochs; supp. Table 1). 'The feature extractor architecture is shared across all transformation methods.'

'The comparison results are calculated over 600 evaluation episodes.' (Sec. 4.2, p. 6). Metrics: 'we use the closed-set classification accuracy (Acc) and the AUROC of unknown class sample detection (AUROC) for evaluation. The accuracy measures the correct classification ratio using the seen class samples, and the AUROC measures unseen class instance detection capability using both seen and unseen class samples.' (Sec. 4.1, p. 6). Open-set score (Algorithm 1, p. 4): c = predicted query class; P^q = P - {p_c} + {q}; d_SnaTCHer = sum_{c in Y^S} dist(p~^q_c, p~_c) where p~ = T(.) are transformed prototypes; 'if d_SnaTCHer > tau then The query is unknown'. 'We utilized Euclidean distance with a temperature value of 64 for the distance function' (Sec. 3.5, p. 6). '±' = 95% confidence interval (Fig. 2 caption: 'Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals'; Table 2/3 captions: 'Please see the supplementary material for the confidence intervals'). Baselines: 'For all FSL methods, we determined the unknown detection score with the negative of the predicted class probability. For OpenMax, we fitted the Weibull models over the training episodes and used them to detect unknowns in the evaluation stage. For NN, we used a ProtoNet-based classifier to calculate logits.' (Sec. 4.4, p. 7). Training: SGD 'over 20,000 episodes' (Sec. 4.2). Datasets: miniImageNet 64/16/20 (split of [24]), tieredImageNet 351/97/160, 84x84.

protocol: Cross-domain FSOSR (Sec. 4.6, p. 8): 'For the unseen data domain, we use the CUB [33] dataset, which is composed of 200 classes of RGB bird images. Similarly, we define a CUB-tieredImageNet case and a CUB-CUB case to assess the generalization capabilities of the FSOSR methods. For the latter two cases, we use the models trained with 5-way 5-shot tieredImageNet episodes for evaluations.' backbone_and_pretraining: ResNet-12; 'We use ResNet12 [19] network as the feature backbone. Following [9,41], we pre-train the ResNet12 and a classifier (a linear layer) with cross-entropy loss and a self-supervised rotation loss on the base set under fully-supervised classification task for 90 epochs using a SGD optimizer with learning rate 0.05 decayed by 10 at epoch 60. The weights in the linear layer are used as base-class many-shot prototypes P* for ATT-G and SEMAN-G.' (Sec. 5.0.2, p. 7176). SEMAN-G additionally uses GloVe word embeddings of class names ('For SEMAN-G, we extract word embedding using GloVe [30]', p. 7176). Supp. Sec. 1: 'all the re-implemented methods use the same feature extractor (ResNet12) as ours, which is first pre-trained on the base set.'
protocol: 5-way: 'During meta-testing, we follow [20, 24] to randomly sample 600 tasks, and report the average value with 95% confidence interval for all the metrics. We use cosine similarity [10] as the similarity function to compute per-class prediction scores. For FSOR evaluation, we follow [24] to sample training and testing tasks, where we set N = 5 and K = 1, 5. For each task, we sample 15 positive queries from each few-shot class. For negative detection, we sample 5 negative classes with each containing 15 negative queries.' (Sec. 5.0.2, p. 7176). Metrics (Sec. 5.0.3, p. 7176): 'we report top-1 accuracy for FSOR tasks over few-shot classes'; 'To measure the negative detection performance, we follow the protocol in [20, 24] to report AUROC (area Under ROC Curve). To measure the overall open-set recognition performance, we follow the protocol in [49] to report macro-averaged F1-scores on all many-shot/few-shot and negative classes.' Rejection rule (Sec. 4.1, p. 7174): theta_a = f_s(f(q), p^-) (Eq. 2); 'a negative query q in Q^n will be rejected if max{f_s(f(q), p_c)}_{c in C^f} < theta_a'; with M = 5 negative prototypes 'the maximum threshold theta_a = max{theta_a,i} is used as the final threshold' (Sec. 4.2.5; 'For the following experiment results, we set M = 5 for our methods', p. 7176). Meta-training: 'The entire network is trained for 18k tasks with a SGD optimizer' (p. 7176). 'All images for the two datasets are sized to 84x84' (mini/tiered); CIFAR-FS/FC100 'all images for the two sets are of size is 32x32' (p. 7178).

For FSOR evaluation, we follow [24] to sample training and testing tasks, where we set N = 5 and K = 1, 5. For each task, we sample 15 positive queries from each few-shot class. For negative detection, we sample 5 negative classes with each containing 15 negative queries.' (Sec. 5.0.2, p. 7176). Metrics (Sec. 5.0.3, p. 7176): 'we report top-1 accuracy for FSOR tasks over few-shot classes'; 'To measure the negative detection performance, we follow the protocol in [20, 24] to report AUROC (area Under ROC Curve). To measure the overall open-set recognition performance, we follow the protocol in [49] to report macro-averaged F1-scores on all many-shot/few-shot and negative classes.' Rejection rule (Sec. 4.1, p. 7174): theta_a = f_s(f(q), p^-) (Eq. 2); 'a negative query q in Q^n will be rejected if max{f_s(f(q), p_c)}_{c in C^f} < theta_a'; with M = 5 negative prototypes 'the maximum threshold theta_a = max{theta_a,i} is used as the final threshold' (Sec. 4.2.5; 'For the following experiment results, we set M = 5 for our methods', p. 7176). Meta-training: 'The entire network is trained for 18k tasks with a SGD optimizer' (p. 7176). 'All images for the two datasets are sized to 84x84' (mini/tiered); CIFAR-FS/FC100 'all images for the two sets are of size is 32x32' (p. 7178).

protocol: 5-way; Table 1 (p. 6, v4) for miniImageNet->miniImageNet: K^c_Qin = 15 in-distribution queries per support class (5-shot and 1-shot), K_Qout = 75 out-of-distribution queries per episode, E_train = 50000, E_test = 600. 'For all our evaluations, we split the query set equally among in-distribution and out-of-distribution samples' (p. 6). 'In order to simulate the presence of out-of-distribution samples, we follow the strategy outlined in [12] and augment the query set with samples from classes absent in the support' (p. 3; [12] = PEELER). Number of open classes per episode is not given in Table 1; the openness study (Table 7, p. 10) states 'N_target refers to the number of open classes we sample Q_out. We vary N_target from 5 to 15' and its 0%-openness column corresponds to N_target = 5, which implies 5 open classes by default (inference). Open-set score: sigmoid output p of the MLP detector fed with [p, z_hat_q, D] ('This MLP classifier outputs a sigmoidal probability value p, indicating the openness of a query sample', p. 5). 'we compute the accuracy over in-distribution queries and utilize the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) to quantify the model's performance in detecting the out-of-distribution samples' (p. 6). 'The performance of all methods is averaged over 600 test episodes and reported with 95% confidence levels' (Table 4 caption, p. 8). Images 84x84.

protocol: Sec. 5.3 (p. 6): 'For a N-way K-shot FSOR task, we following previous FSOR methods [6, 13, 15, 18] to select 2N classes in the dataset, half of which are known classes and the other are unknown classes. During the testing phase, the first 75 query samples with the highest open-set scores (i.e., the energy score in Eq. 15) are taken as open-set samples to calculate the open-set recognition metrics.' (5-way: 5 known + 5 unknown classes, 75 known + 75 unknown queries.) Sec. 5.2 (p. 5): 'ACC ... dividing the number of correctly classified samples in Q_k by the number of samples in Q_k. venue_year: CVPR 2023, pp. 24007-24016 (Boudiaf, Bennequin, Tami, Toubhans, Piantanida, Hudelot, Ben Ayed); arXiv:2301.08390v2 (19 May 2023). The requester said ICCV 2023: the CVF open-access PDF is in the CVPR 2023 proceedings.
backbone_and_pretraining: ResNet-12; Off-the-shelf pre-trained ResNet-12 checkpoint released by the FEAT authors [48], trained on the base classes of the respective dataset (Sec. 5.1 'Architectures and checkpoints', p. 24012: 'all non-episodic methods are tuned and tested using off-the-shelf pre-trained checkpoints. All results except fig:barplots are produced using the pre-trained ResNet-12 and Wide-ResNet 28-10 checkpoints provided by the authors from [48]'). Feature extractor frozen; features center-normalized.
protocol: 5-way episodes. Sec. 5.1 'Datasets and tasks' (p. 24012): 'Following standard FSOSR protocol, support sets contain |CCS| = 5 closed-set classes with 1 or 5 instances, or shots, per class, and query sets are formed by sampling 15 instances per class, from a total of ten classes: the five closed-set classes and an additional set of |COS| = 5 open-set classes. We follow this setting for a fair comparison with previous works [16, 21] which sample open-set query instances from only 5 classes. We also report results in supplementary materials for a more general setting in which open-set query instances are sampled indifferently from all remaining classes in the test set.' => per episode 5 known classes x 15 queries = 75 inlier queries + 5 open-set classes x 15 queries = 75 outlier queries (|Q| = 150). Appendix E (arXiv v2, p. 12) 'broad open-set setting' (Fig. 6 only): 'the query set is formed by sampling 15 instances for each of the 5 closed-set classes, plus 5 x 15 = 75 open-set instances, which are sampled indifferently from all remaining classes in the test set.' Open-set score for baselines (p. 24010): 'Following [16], closed-set few-shot classifiers are turned into open-set classifiers by considering the negative of the maximum probability as a measure of outlierness.' OSLO's own score is the latent outlierness 1 - xi_i ('providing a principled outlierness score, as 1 - xi_i', p. 24011). Metrics (arXiv v2 Appendix C, p. 12): 'Acc: the classification accuracy on the closed-set instances of the query set (i.e. yq in CS)'; 'AUROC: ... For a set of outlier predictions in [0, 1] and their ground truth (0 for inliers, 1 for outliers), any threshold ... gives a true positive rate ... and a false positive rate ... The area under this curve is a measure of the discrimination ability of the outlier detector'; AUPR and Prec@0.9 (precision at 90% recall) are also reported; 'Random predictions lead to an AUPR equal to the proportion of outliers in the query set i.e. 50% in our set-up' => AUROC is computed per episode over all 150 queries (75 inliers vs 75 outliers). Features (p. 24010-24011): 'applying a center-normalize transformation ... on the features extracted by [phi] benefited all methods ... using an inductive Base centering [42] for inductive methods ... and a transductive Task centering [14] ... for all transductive methods'. Hyper-parameters: 'we define a grid over salient hyper-parameters and tune over the validation split of mini-ImageNet ... we then keep hyper-parameters fixed across all other experiments' (p. 24012). Number of test episodes: NOT stated in the main paper nor in the arXiv appendix. Variance: Table 1 caption 'For each column, a light-gray standard deviation is indicated, corresponding to the maximum deviation observed across methods for that metric' (mini 1-shot: Acc +-0.72, AUROC +-0.79, AUPR +-0.69, Prec@0.9 +-0.47; mini 5-shot: +-0.44, +-0.73, +-0.61, +-0.56; tiered 1-shot: +-0.74, +-0.76, +-0.71, +-0.52; tiered 5-shot: +-0.52, +-0.68, +-0.75, +-0.57).

Sec. 5.1 'Datasets and tasks' (p. 24012): 'Following standard FSOSR protocol, support sets contain |CCS| = 5 closed-set classes with 1 or 5 instances, or shots, per class, and query sets are formed by sampling 15 instances per class, from a total of ten classes: the five closed-set classes and an additional set of |COS| = 5 open-set classes. We follow this setting for a fair comparison with previous works [16, 21] which sample open-set query instances from only 5 classes. We also report results in supplementary materials for a more general setting in which open-set query instances are sampled indifferently from all remaining classes in the test set.' => per episode 5 known classes x 15 queries = 75 inlier queries + 5 open-set classes x 15 queries = 75 outlier queries (|Q| = 150). Appendix E (arXiv v2, p. 12) 'broad open-set setting' (Fig. 6 only): 'the query set is formed by sampling 15 instances for each of the 5 closed-set classes, plus 5 x 15 = 75 open-set instances, which are sampled indifferently from all remaining classes in the test set.' Open-set score for baselines (p. 24010): 'Following [16], closed-set few-shot classifiers are turned into open-set classifiers by considering the negative of the maximum probability as a measure of outlierness.' OSLO's own score is the latent outlierness 1 - xi_i ('providing a principled outlierness score, as 1 - xi_i', p. 24011). Metrics (arXiv v2 Appendix C, p. 12): 'Acc: the classification accuracy on the closed-set instances of the query set (i.e. yq in CS)'; 'AUROC: ... For a set of outlier predictions in [0, 1] and their ground truth (0 for inliers, 1 for outliers), any threshold ... gives a true positive rate ... and a false positive rate ... The area under this curve is a measure of the discrimination ability of the outlier detector'; AUPR and Prec@0.9 (precision at 90% recall) are also reported; 'Random predictions lead to an AUPR equal to the proportion of outliers in the query set i.e. 50% in our set-up' => AUROC is computed per episode over all 150 queries (75 inliers vs 75 outliers). Features (p. 24010-24011): 'applying a center-normalize transformation ... on the features extracted by [phi] benefited all methods ... using an inductive Base centering [42] for inductive methods ... and a transductive Task centering [14] ... for all transductive methods'. Hyper-parameters: 'we define a grid over salient hyper-parameters and tune over the validation split of mini-ImageNet ... we then keep hyper-parameters fixed across all other experiments' (p. 24012). Number of test episodes: NOT stated in the main paper nor in the arXiv appendix. backbone_and_pretraining: CLIP ViT-B/16; CLIP ViT-B/16 (Radford et al. 2021) with frozen image and text encoders; learned parameters: context prompt vectors (P = 16 tokens, dual context) and the unknown-text combination weights W over F = 100 PCA basis vectors of 1000 base-class word embeddings (U2WO); trained on 16 shots per known class with SGD lr 0.002, cosine schedule, 50 epochs, batch 32 (Sec. 4.1 'Implementation Details', p. 661). Unknown-text length M = 30 per Sec. 4.1 (Supp. S2 says 'is set to 20'). Sec. 4.2: 'For fairness, all methods are trained using the same pre-trained model (CLIP/ViT-B/16), and we reproduce results from M-Tuning [19], ID-like [1], LoCoOp [28], NegPrompt [18].'
benchmark: other: other: iNaturalist (200 known / 800 unknown classes)
protocol: NOT episodic and NOT 5-way: a single known/unknown class split per dataset with 16 training shots per known class. Supp. S2 (p. 1): 'MiniImageNet (MiniIN) [41]: Sixty-four known classes and thirty-six unknown classes are used for evaluation. MiniImageNet contains one hundred classes, and the classes are split as (64, 16, 20) for meta-training, meta-validation, and meta-testing, respectively. Each class has six hundred images. We extended the split as (64, 16+20) for known and unknown classes, respectively. TieredImageNet (TieredIN) [34]: Three hundred fifty-one known classes and two hundred fifty-seven unknown classes are used for evaluation. TieredImageNet contains six hundred eight classes, split into (351, 97, and 160). We extended the split as (351, 97+160) for evaluation.' Large-scale: 'ImageNet-200 (IN-200) [43]: ... the first 200 classes of the ImageNet-1k dataset [7] as known and the remaining 800 ones as the unknown. iNaturalist (iNa) [39]: ... randomly select 200 classes as known classes and the remaining 800 classes as unknown. ImageNet-Easy (IN-Easy) and ImageNet-Hard (IN-Hard) [40]: ... The known is ImagNet-1k. The unknown samples are chosen from the disjoint set of ImageNet-21K-P [35] ... Each unknown set includes 1000 categories. ImageNet-LT (IN-LT) [21]: ... includes 1000 known classes from ImageNet-2012, and 360 unknown classes from the validation set of ImageNet-2010. Places365-Standard [23]: 365 scene classes split as (100, 265).' Metrics: ACC on known samples, AUROC over known + unknown samples (Supp. S2, p. 2); score = MLS on the challenging benchmarks (Supp. S7, p. 5: 'we adapt the MSP score on the standard FSOR benchmark and the MLS score on the challenging benchmark'). Number of test images / episodes: not stated (no episodes; single split). Hyper-parameters: epsilon 0.1 (0.001 for IN-Hard, IN-LT, IN-Easy per Sec. 4.3), N = 5 unknown texts (30 for IN-Hard, 60 for IN-LT).

backbone_and_pretraining: CLIP ViT-B/16; CLIP ViT-B/16 (Radford et al. 2021) with frozen image and text encoders; learned parameters: context prompt vectors (P = 16 tokens, dual context) and the unknown-text combination weights W over F = 100 PCA basis vectors of 1000 base-class word embeddings (U2WO); trained on 16 shots per known class with SGD lr 0.002, cosine schedule, 50 epochs, batch 32 (Sec. 4.1 'Implementation Details', p. 661). Unknown-text length M = 30 per Sec. 4.1 (Supp. S2 says 'is set to 20'). Sec. 4.2: 'For fairness, all methods are trained using the same pre-trained model (CLIP/ViT-B/16), and we reproduce results from M-Tuning [19], ID-like [1], LoCoOp [28], NegPrompt [18].'
benchmark: other: other: ImageNet-200 (200 known / 800 unknown ImageNet-1k classes)
protocol: NOT episodic and NOT 5-way: a single known/unknown class split per dataset with 16 training shots per known class. Supp. S2 (p. 1): 'MiniImageNet (MiniIN) [41]: Sixty-four known classes and thirty-six unknown classes are used for evaluation. MiniImageNet contains one hundred classes, and the classes are split as (64, 16, 20) for meta-training, meta-validation, and meta-testing, respectively. Each class has six hundred images. We extended the split as (64, 16+20) for known and unknown classes, respectively. TieredImageNet (TieredIN) [34]: Three hundred fifty-one known classes and two hundred fifty-seven unknown classes are used for evaluation. TieredImageNet contains six hundred eight classes, split into (351, 97, and 160). We extended the split as (351, 97+160) for evaluation.' Large-scale: 'ImageNet-200 (IN-200) [43]: ... the first 200 classes of the ImageNet-1k dataset [7] as known and the remaining 800 ones as the unknown. iNaturalist (iNa) [39]: ... randomly select 200 classes as known classes and the remaining 800 classes as unknown. ImageNet-Easy (IN-Easy) and ImageNet-Hard (IN-Hard) [40]: ... The known is ImagNet-1k. The unknown samples are chosen from the disjoint set of ImageNet-21K-P [35] ... Each unknown set includes 1000 categories. ImageNet-LT (IN-LT) [21]: ... includes 1000 known classes from ImageNet-2012, and 360 unknown classes from the validation set of ImageNet-2010. Places365-Standard [23]: 365 scene classes split as (100, 265).' Metrics: ACC on known samples, AUROC over known + unknown samples (Supp. S2, p. 2); score = MLS on the challenging benchmarks (Supp. S7, p. 5: 'we adapt the MSP score on the standard FSOR benchmark and the MLS score on the challenging benchmark'). Number of test images / episodes: not stated (no episodes; single split). Hyper-parameters: epsilon 0.1 (0.001 for IN-Hard, IN-LT, IN-Easy per Sec. 4.3), N = 5 unknown texts (30 for IN-Hard, 60 for IN-LT).

backbone_and_pretraining: CLIP RN50; CLIP RN50 frozen encoders with the same prompt-learning recipe (Supp. S6 'Additional Results with Backbone of RN50', p. 4).
protocol: NOT episodic and NOT 5-way: OSR-style class splits with 16 training shots per known class ('16-shot setting'). Supp. S2 (p. 1): 'CIFAR10 (C10) [16]: Six known classes and four unknown classes are randomly sampled. CIFAR10 + 10 (C10 + 10), CIFAR10 + 50 (C10 + 50): For the CIFAR10 + N experiments, four classes from CIFAR10 are used for training, while N classes from CIFAR100 [16] are used for evaluation, where N denotes either 10 or 50 classes. CIFAR100 (C100) [16]: Twenty known classes and eighty unknown classes are randomly sampled. TinyImageNet (TINY) [17]: Twenty known classes and one hundred eighty unknown classes are randomly sampled for evaluation. TinyImageNet-Hard (TINY-H) [17]: Forty known classes and one hundred sixty unknown classes are randomly sampled for evaluation. The above six benchmarks are evaluated over five random splits.' Main paper Sec. 4.1 (p. 661): 'All results on the six traditional benchmarks are reported over five random splits on average.' (+- = std over the five splits, as printed). Metrics (Supp. S2, p. 2): 'we evaluate the model's closed-set performance with accuracy (ACC) and evaluate the open performance with the area under the ROC curve (AUROC) for unknown class detection. The closed-set performance is the classification capacity via known samples, and the open performance is the unknown detection capacity via both known and unknown samples.' OSCR also reported (Table S6). Score: MSP of the open-set softmax p^O (Eq. 4, which includes the N unknown-text logits in the denominator); Supp. S7 (p. 5): 'we adapt the MSP score on the standard FSOR benchmark and the MLS score on the challenging benchmark.' Number of test images: the full test split of the known + unknown classes (no episodes; count not stated).

Test episodes: 'The comparison results are obtained through 1,000 evaluation episodes with 1,000 tasks per episode and computed the mean over 1,000 episodes.' (Sec. 5.1, p. 7-8). (Sec. 5.1 'Datasets and tasks', p. 7). Number of test tasks/episodes: NOT stated anywhere in the paper (deviation from the usual '600 episodes' statement). Outlier score for closed-set classifiers: 'Following [17], closed-set few-shot classifiers are turned into open-set classifiers by considering the negative of the maximum probability as a measure of outlierness.' (Sec. 5.1, p. 6). Features are center-normalised before every method: 'an inductive Base centering [40] for inductive methods ... and a transductive Task centering [16] ... for all transductive methods' (p. 6). Hyperparameters: 'For all methods, we define a grid over salient hyper-parameters and tune over the validation split of mini-ImageNet.' (p. 6). Metrics (Appendix A, p. 12): 'Acc: the classification accuracy on the closed-set instances of the query set'; AUROC; AUPR; 'Prec@0.9: the precision at 90% recall'; 'Random predictions lead to an AUPR equal to the proportion of outliers in the query set i.e., 50% in our set-up.' The +/- printed under each column header is NOT a per-method interval: 'For each column, a light-gray standard deviation is indicated, corresponding to the maximum deviation observed across methods for that metric.' (Table 2/4 captions). Column-wise max std, Table 2 (mini): Acc +/-0.72, AUROC +/-0.79, AUPR +/-0.69, Prec@0.9 +/-0.47 (1-shot); +/-0.44, +/-0.73, +/-0.61, +/-0.56 (5-shot). backbone_and_pretraining: ResNet-12 (frozen after FEAT pre-training; exponential map to hyperbolic space on top); Sec. 5.2.2 'Implementation details', p. 14: 'we use ResNet-12 (He et al, 2016) as the feature extractor of our network. We first use FEAT to pre-train the backbone on the training set, then remove the last fully connected layer and the softmax layer. The remaining layers are fixed and used as feature extractors in our meta-learning process.'
protocol: Sec. 5.2.2, p. 14: 'For an N-way K-shot FSOR task, we follow previous FSOR methods (Deng et al, 2022; Huang et al, 2022; Jeong et al, 2021) to select 2N classes in the dataset, half of which are seen classes and the other are unseen classes. For seen classes, we sample K images for each class as a support set and another 15 images as a seen query set. For each unseen class, we only sample 15 images as an unseen query set. ... During the testing phase, the first 75 query samples with the highest open-set scores are taken as open-set samples to calculate the open-set recognition metrics.' => 5 known + 5 unknown classes, 15 queries each. Number of TEST episodes: NOT stated (only 'over 60,000 tasks' of meta-training, p. 15). Metrics (p. 14): 'ACC ... dividing the number of correctly classified samples in Q_s by the number of samples in Q_s. AUROC ... the area under the ROC curve for open-set recognition of all query samples Q_s ∪ Q_u.' ± printed; CI type not stated in Sec. 5.2.

backbone_and_pretraining: ResNet-12 (640-d) + hypernetwork H (2-layer MLP, 256 units) generating the classifier; Sec. 5.2, p. 5: 'we train F using a combination of supervised and self-supervised criteria. In the pre-training stage, a stack of two linear classifiers are learned on top of F, where the first classifier predicts the class logits ŷ for the |C_b|-way classification task, and the second classifier predicts the rotation logits r̂.'; hypernetwork meta-trained 50 epochs × 200 batches (p. 6).
protocol: Sec. 5.2 'Evaluation Protocol', p. 6: 'We sample 400 episodes randomly from the meta-test set containing novel classes C_n that the model has not previously encountered. In each episode, the model is given a labeled support set of KN samples that is referred to as the IND samples, and a set of 20 unlabeled queries. Of the 20 queries, 10 belong to the N IND classes and the remaining 10 are OOD. In our experiments, we consider the near-OOD detection task ... we reserve classes from the same dataset as OOD during evaluation. In our experiments, we consider the classes outside a given episode as OOD during evaluation.' Shots: '5-shot 5-way' and '10-shot 5-way' (NO 1-shot). Metrics: IND Acc (N-way accuracy on IND queries), AUROC and FPR@90 for the binary OOD task, score = max softmax probability. DEVIATIONS from standard FSOR: 400 test episodes (not 600); 20 queries per episode in total (10 IND + 10 OOD; not 15 per class); OOD queries come from all remaining meta-test classes rather than 5 fixed unknown classes; 10-shot replaces 1-shot.
